text:
ingrid: Short convergence thread after prototyping lazy-reuse + soft-compact + hole-preserve. Want to align on a simple controller that balances warmness reuse vs fragmentation. Thoughts?

nate: From proto numbers, reuse reduced host allocs by ~28% on bursty traces but increased medium-span fragmentation ~6%. We need a controller to trade those.

yuki: Agree. My rough idea: single adaptive controller per-pool that exposes two knobs: reuse_window and preserve_ms, and drives them by two signals: alloc_failure_rate and tail_latency.

tom: Can we make the controller rules deterministic and explainable? e.g., if alloc_failure_rate > A then decay reuse_window *= 0.7 and shrink preserve_ms; if tail_latency > B then increase reuse_window *= 1.1. Simple PID-ish.

ingrid: Yes, keep it simple initially. Also we should prioritize eviction of preserved entries when a large allocation comes in (so we don't block big spans).

nate: One operational quirk: on heterogeneous tenants some pools see heavy churn. Controller should use tenant-scoped metrics when available or fall back to pool-level aggregates.

yuki: Proposal for signals (telemetry):
- reuse.hits, reuse.misses, reuse.expired
- preserved.count, preserved.hits, preserved.evicted
- softcompact.merges, softcompact.scans, softcompact.time_ms
- alloc.fail_rate, alloc.tail_p50/95/99, alloc.large_failures

tom: We also need heat-aware scoring: only put spans with warmness >= W into reuse/preserve reservoirs. That prevents keeping cold garbage. Warmness derived from recent touch counts and last-touch recency.

ingrid: Implementation detail: controller tick (every 250ms?) collects sliding-window signals. Rules:
1) If alloc.fail_rate > 0.5% OR alloc.large_failures rising -> reduce reuse_window by factor f_down (0.7) and set preserve_ms=min_ms.
2) Else if tail_p99 < tail_target and reuse.hit_rate < target -> increase reuse_window f_up (1.05) up to max.
3) Soft-compact runs only if compact_allowed && softcompact_made_progress_recently < threshold. Compact_allowed = tail_p95 < compact_tail_thresh AND queue_depth_low.

nate: 250ms tick seems OK, but we should allow operator override and a conservative default for Dedicated (off). Also a global kill-switch for incidents.

yuki: Edge-case: controller oscillation. Add hysteresis: only update if metric delta exceeds epsilon for N ticks. Also clamp rate of change per minute.

tom: Sketch pseudocode for controller: 

/* run on pool controller tick */
void controller_tick(pool) {
  metrics = sample_pool_metrics(pool);
  if (metrics.alloc_fail_rate > pool.cfg.fail_thresh) {
    pool.cfg.reuse_window = max(pool.cfg.min_reuse, pool.cfg.reuse_window * 0.7);
    pool.cfg.preserve_ms = pool.cfg.min_preserve;
  } else if (metrics.tail_p99 < pool.cfg.lat_target && metrics.reuse_hit_rate < pool.cfg.hit_target) {
    pool.cfg.reuse_window = min(pool.cfg.max_reuse, pool.cfg.reuse_window * 1.05);
  }
  // compact gating
  pool.compact_allowed = (metrics.tail_p95 < pool.cfg.compact_tail_thresh) && (metrics.queue_depth < pool.cfg.queue_thresh);
}

yuki: Nice. For observability: emit controller decisions as events and expose current cfg via runtime API /pools/<id>/config so SRE can inspect.

ingrid: Testing plan: 
- microbench: synthetic bursts with warm-hot key reuse; compare reuse on/off, preserve on/off, softcompaction on/off.
- regression: heavy multi-tenant churn + large allocation bursts to ensure controller reduces reuse_window and avoids allocation storms.
- long-soak: 6h run with default controller.

nate: Also instrument allocation trace sampling (low-sample-rate) to validate we aren't keeping a span longer than desired and that eviction paths are exercised.

tom: Security/tenant isolation note: preserved/reuse reservoirs must be tenant-tagged. For pools without tenant id (shared infra) we should bias towards short windows.

infra-bot: controller-tick scheduled for pool gpu-4 every 250ms :gear: 

yuki: One more thought: allow explicit per-route hints from the prefetcher or runtime to temporarily pin a span for reuse beyond reuse_window (e.g., during a model hotload). That should be opt-in by route.

ingrid: Good idea. We'll add a route-level API: request_reuse_reservation(span, duration) which increments a reservation counter and bypasses reuse expiry. Only privileged subsystems can call.

nate: Any objections to the default parameters? my suggested defaults: reuse_window=500ms, preserve_ms=300ms, max_reuse_span=256KB, min_reuse=50ms. Dedicated=off, Private=opt-in.

tom: Sounds conservative. +1 from me.

yuki: +1. I'll add the telemetry dashboard tiles and controller debug logs we talked about.

ingrid: I'll open the RFC follow-up PR with controller code, telemetry list, and perf harness. I'll include knobs, route hint API, and tests. Thanks everyone.

nate: :thumbsup:

tom: LGTM

yuki: Will review PR.
